questions.stem: A rate limiter starts with `int limit = 0;` and runs `switch (tier) { case 1: limit = 10; break; default: audit.add("tier " + tier); case 2: limit = 100; break; case 3: limit = 1000; }`. A request arrives with tier 7. What happens?

options.text: "tier 7" is audited and limit stays 0, since the statements under default end where the next label begins
options.says: a label is only an entry point; execution runs on through later labels until a break

options.text: "tier 7" is audited and limit becomes 100, since the statements under default run on into the ones below them
options.says: default is entered for 7 and, with no break, execution continues into case 2's statements until its break

options.text: The class doesn't compile, since the statements under default would run on into another case's statements
options.says: fall-through compiles; javac warns about it only with -Xlint:fallthrough

options.text: The class doesn't compile, since default has to be the last label of a switch statement
options.says: default can stand anywhere among the labels; its position doesn't change which values reach it

origin.section: A Case Label Is Where Execution Enters, and It Runs On Until a break

questions.stem: A retry policy declares `static final Integer MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5;` and `static final int WARN_AT = 3;`. A switch on `int attempt` uses `case WARN_AT:` and `case MAX_ATTEMPTS:`. What does javac do with it?

options.text: It accepts both labels, since both fields are static, final and set from a literal
options.says: final is not enough: a constant variable has a primitive or String type, and an Integer field is neither

options.text: It accepts both labels, since the Integer field is unboxed to an int where the label is compared
options.says: labels are fixed in the compiled table, so a label must be a constant expression; javac reports 'constant expression required' for the Integer field

options.text: It rejects the MAX_ATTEMPTS label, since a field of a wrapper type is not a constant expression
options.says: an int field initialised with a literal is a constant; an Integer field is not, so its label is 'constant expression required'

options.text: It rejects the MAX_ATTEMPTS label, since an Integer label doesn't match the type of an int selector
options.says: Integer labels on an int selector are not the problem; javac reports 'constant expression required', because a final field of a wrapper type is not a constant

origin.section: The Selector Is an int-Compatible Type, a String or an Enum, and Every Label Is a Distinct Constant

questions.stem: A method reads `switch (region) { case "eu": return Region.EU; case "us": return Region.US; case "apac": return Region.APAC; } throw new IllegalArgumentException(region);`. To stop a NullPointerException from rows with no region, a developer adds `case null: return Region.EU;` as the first label. What happens when the class is compiled with Java 21?

options.text: It compiles, and a null region now returns EU, since case null is matched before the selector is hashed
options.says: the compiler refuses this switch: with case null it must cover every value, and it has no default

options.text: It compiles, and a null region still throws, since the selector is hashed before any label is matched
options.says: the switch doesn't compile at all; where case null is accepted, it handles a null selector instead of throwing

options.text: It fails to compile, since a switch with case null has to cover every value, and these labels don't
options.says: case null makes the compiler require full coverage of the selector; without a default javac reports 'does not cover all possible input values'

options.text: It fails to compile, since case null is allowed in a switch expression, and this is a switch statement
options.says: Java 21 allows case null in a switch statement too; the error is about coverage

origin.section: A null Selector Throws Before Any Label Is Compared, default Included

questions.stem: `enum Plan { FREE, TEAM, BUSINESS }`. A billing class has a switch statement that names all three constants and no default. A release adds ENTERPRISE to the enum, and only the enum's file is recompiled. What does the billing switch do for an ENTERPRISE customer?

options.text: It runs no case and carries on after the switch, since the old switch class finds each constant by name
options.says: a classic switch statement over an enum is not checked for coverage, and the old class still matches constants by name, so ENTERPRISE matches no label

options.text: It runs no case and throws after the switch, since the old switch class meets a constant it was not compiled with
options.says: a classic switch statement has no hidden default that throws: a value no label names runs nothing

options.text: It runs the BUSINESS case, since the old switch class sends a constant it has no label for to its last label
options.says: a value no label names enters no case; without a default nothing runs

options.text: It runs the FREE case, since the old switch class sends a constant it has no label for to its first label
options.says: a value no label names enters no case; without a default nothing runs

origin.section: A Switch Statement Over an Enum Needn't Name Every Constant, So a New Constant Runs Nothing
